results.content:
Everyone loves a sporting record, even if it’s set by your bitter rivals, overtime sports fans learn to look back upon it with grudging appreciation. An unbeaten run is always a big deal in football, especially in the English Premier League where competition is ferocious.  
What is the longest unbeaten streak in Premier League history? **The longest unbeaten streak in Premier League history was set by Arsenal between May 7th 2003 and October 16th 2004. Spanning 3 seasons, Arsenal’s 49 game unbeaten [run](https://soccernoise.com/how-far-do-premier-league-players-run-in-a-game/) saw them go undefeated for an entire season (2003-04) which saw them win the title. That Arsenal side became known as the Invincibles.**
## **The longest unbeaten league run in football history**  
Now that we have looked at the best unbeaten runs in English football, let’s see how the rest of the world get on.  
Italian giants AC Milan have the longest unbeaten run in football history. The *Rossoneri* went 58 league games without defeat. In Italy, similar to Arsenal in England, they are known as “Gli invincibili ” (The invincibles). The unbeaten streak ran between 1991 and 1993. It spanned two coaches, Arrigo Sacchi and Fabio Capello, three Serie A titles 1992, 1993 and 1994. The team featured all-time legends such as Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi, Carlo Ancelotti, Marco Van Basten and Guiseppi Signori. In the 1991-1992 season, Milan won just 22 games drawing 12 but were still able to win Serie A.
## **The longest winning run in football history**  
Going unbeaten is all well and good, but drawing is like kissing your sister, or so they say. German juggernaut Bayern Munich set the longest winning streak in football, winning 23 straight matches in the 2019/2021 season. The streak was ignited by the appointment of head coach Hansi Flick took over after the dismissal of Niko Kovac. Bayern Munich would go on to win the Bundesliga, the DFB Pokal and a sixth club Champions League trophy.

results.name: 12 Longest Unbeaten Runs in Premier League History (Ranked)
results.content:
The [Premier League](https://www.givemesport.com/tag/premier-league/) has seen some of the best sides created and then go on long unbeaten runs, with some in the process achieving greatness. During the inaugural season of the Football League back in 1888/89, Preston North End completed the [entire campaign unbeaten](https://www.givemesport.com/football-soccer-whole-league-season-unbeaten), a record that no club in England's top flight would emulate for the next 115 years.  
Many thought at the time that it would never happen again before Arsenal's Invincibles came along. The Gunners remain the only side in Premier League history to avoid a single defeat throughout the whole campaign. However, the north London outfit are not the only club in the modern history of the division to have forgotten what a loss feels like.  
Here's a closer look at the longest unbeaten runs in Premier League history, featuring the familiar roll call of legendary clubs and one or two unexpected vintages.
## 10 **Liverpool - 26**  
### **September 2024 - April 2025**  
Arne Slot's debut season in charge at Anfield couldn't have gone much better. Replacing Jurgen Klopp was never going to be easy, but the Dutchman settled in very quickly and pushed the Reds to the top of the Premier League. It's a spot they've rarely relinquished either and with the campaign almost complete now, they've tasted defeat just twice in the league. His first defeat came against Nottingham Forest fairly early, but his side then went on a 26-match unbeaten run, solidifying their spot at the top of the table.  
They look almost certain to lift the trophy for just the second time ever, but their charge to the gold took a small hit when they were surprisingly defeated by Fulham at Craven Cottage in April. It came out of nowhere, but the club still managed to go 26 games without a loss, one of the longest streaks in Premier League history.

|---|---|
| **Games Unbeaten** | 26 |
| **Biggest Win** | Liverpool 5-0 West Ham United |
| **Run Ended By** | Fulham |
## 6 **Manchester City – 30**  
### **April 2017–January 2018**  
It's of little surprise to see another Pep Guardiola side on this list. This was a memorable season for Manchester City, [breaking several Premier League records](https://theanalyst.com/eu/2023/07/the-longest-unbeaten-runs-in-the-premier-league/) along the way. City racked up the most points in a Premier League season (100), most away points (50), most wins (32) and most consecutive victories (18).  
City's unbeaten run had some incredible results including a 5-0 victory over Liverpool at the Etihad Stadium, a 6-0 win away at Watford and a 7-2 pummelling of Stoke City. Their glittering sequence came to an end in a 4-3 thriller at Anfield in January 2018, one of just two Premier League defeats throughout the memorable campaign.

The Premier League, renowned for its competitive nature, has witnessed some remarkable unbeaten streaks. Teams that manage to remain undefeated for an extended period not only secure their place in history but also showcase tactical brilliance, depth, and consistency. Among these, Arsenal’s “Invincibles” season of 2003–2004 stands as a landmark achievement. However, other teams have also etched their names into the records. Let’s explore the longest unbeaten runs in Premier League history, analyzing the strategies and resilience behind these remarkable feats.
## The Unbeaten Runs: A Historical Perspective

Arsenal’s 49-game unbeaten streak remains unmatched in Premier League history. Key players like Thierry Henry, Patrick Vieira, and Robert Pires were instrumental in maintaining this legendary run. Their unbeaten streak spanned across multiple seasons, including the entirety of the 2003–2004 campaign, earning them the iconic “Invincibles” title.

results.name: The Premier League’s Longest Unbeaten Runs: Overall, Home, and Away - PremierLeagueNow
results.content:
Unbeaten runs are a special kind of achievement. Winning titles requires consistency, but going unbeaten across long stretches of a Premier League season — or multiple seasons — is a different level of dominance. These streaks showcase resilience, tactical clarity, and mental strength. They tell the story not just of a team’s quality, but its refusal to lose even on off-days.  
Across Premier League history, several sides have put together remarkable unbeaten records. Some did it with free-flowing attacking football, others through defensive discipline, and a few through pure force of will. Here, we look at the longest overall unbeaten streaks, plus the most impressive home and away runs the league has ever seen.
## **The Longest Home Unbeaten Runs**  
### **Chelsea’s Stamford Bridge Fortress**  
The longest home unbeaten run in Premier League history belongs to Chelsea. Between 2004 and 2008, they went an astonishing 86 Premier League home games without defeat. Stamford Bridge became a true fortress; visiting teams often seemed beaten before the match even kicked off.
What makes this streak especially remarkable is that it spanned multiple managers and tactical changes. Regardless of who stood in the dugout, Chelsea’s home form remained unshakeable. Their combination of physicality, structure, and game management made breaking them down a near-impossible task.
## **The Longest Away Unbeaten Runs**  
### **Manchester United – Road Warriors**  
The longest away unbeaten run in Premier League history belongs to Manchester United, who went [29 away matches without defeat](https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/701816-longest-unbeaten-away-run-in-the-football-soccer-english-premier-league). Achieved across parts of the 2020–21 period, this run stands out because winning or avoiding defeat away from home is often the hardest task in the league.
Crowd hostility, tactical challenges, and physical fatigue make away runs especially impressive. United’s mixture of defensive solidity, counter-attacking strength, and mental resilience carried them through countless tight matches where a slip could have ended the streak.

In 2003/04, Arsenal became the first team to complete a Premier League season unbeaten, but how long was their unbeaten run in the end? And who else has put together the longest unbeaten runs? Read on to find out...  
**Team (date)****Unbeaten run**Arsenal (May ’03—Oct ’04)49 gamesLiverpool (Jan ‘19—Feb ‘20)44 gamesChelsea (Oct ’04 —Oct ‘05)40 gamesArsenal (Dec ’01—Oct ’02)30 gamesManchester City (Apr ’17—Jan ’18)30 games  
Arsenal’s unbeaten run actually spanned three seasons, from the end of the 2002/03 campaign through to the early stages of the 2004/05 term.  
The Gunners’ legendary run however very nearly ended before it had begun, when Manchester United were given a stoppage-time penalty at Old Trafford with the score 0-0, only for the ultra-reliable Ruud van Nistelrooy to see his effort smash off the crossbar.  
It was as close as Arsenal would come to losing that season, and they took 25 points from a possible 27 to start the following campaign before returning to Old Trafford.  
If they had a slice of luck in the previous year’s clash, they had none in 2005. On the wrong end of a number of contentious refereeing decisions, a harshly awarded penalty – this time converted by Van Nistelrooy – and a late Wayne Rooney goal was enough to bring the run to a halt.
Prior to Arsenal’s 49-game run, it was actually the Gunners who held the previous record with 30. A resurgent Arsenal were unbeaten for the whole second half of the 2001/02 campaign, winning the final 13 games to overhaul Manchester United, winning the title at Old Trafford no less.  
The Gunners were unbeaten in their first nine games of the 2002/03 season, becoming the first side to go unbeaten for 30 games (eclipsing Manchester United’s record of 29), when a 16-year-old Rooney came off the bench to end the Gunners’ streak.  
The arrival of Jose Mourinho at Stamford Bridge signalled a new era in West London, with the Blues almost impossible to beat under the Portuguese. Chelsea would lose their ninth game of the season to Manchester City, but wouldn’t lose again, going a full 12 months unbeaten – a run that eventually stretched to 40 games.  
In 2018, Manchester City’s Centurions became the fourth side to reach 30 games unbeaten, and having taken 62 points from a possible 66, the question was whether they could go the whole season unbeaten. Liverpool, however, dashed City’s dreams when a 10-minute spell saw Liverpool score three goals and end the would-be-champions’ run.
Liverpool themselves looked set for an unbeaten season in 2020. Having pushed Manchester City all the way the previous term, amassing 97 points, the Reds won 26 of their first 27 games, drawing to Manchester United. But an inspired performance from Watford saw the Hornets score three times in a little over 15 minutes to end their run five short of Arsenal’s record.

Palace last lost a match on April 16 — 5-0 away at Newcastle United — and since then have gone 18 unbeaten across five competitions to move level with the team from 1969. How would it compare to the other current Premier League clubs’ record runs without defeat in all competitions? What is the longest an English side has ever gone without losing? And which team’s best streak came in the 19th century?
Chelsea’s joint-longest unbeaten run ended in Wigan (Andrew Yates/AFP via Getty Images) Aston Villa are the only current Premier League club whose record streak without losing took place in the 19th century.
Their 26 games without losing in 1998 under Peter Reid came as a second-tier side and, unsurprisingly, helped them get promoted to the Premier League at the end of the 1998-99 campaign. The second match of the run was the play-off final, which concluded their 1997-98 season, with Sunderland drawing with Charlton Athletic before being defeated in the tie-breaking penalty shootout. Liverpool’s 25-game unbeaten run, which culminated in November 2021, tied their record from 1982, with both streaks ended by a single-goal margin in a league match the weekend after a home victory in the European Cup/Champions League.
The shortest unbeaten runs by clubs currently in the Premier League are the 17-game streaks for Brentford and Brighton respectively.
